newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesian pulp firm signs $991 million loan.
newsitem.headline: Indonesian pulp firm signs $991 million loan.

text.p: Indonesian timber tycoon Prajogo Pangestu signed a $991 million loan agreement with foreign banks on Friday to finance a new pulp plant and pledged the mill will be environmentally sound.
"We can call the pulp project green-friendly because we have already planted the trees for reforestation," Prajogo told reporters after the signing of the loan.
A unit of Prajogo's timber company PT Barito Pacific, PT Tanjung Enim Lestari Pulp and Paper, signed the loan agreement with 25 foreign banks for setting up the new pulp mill, he said.
Prajogo said the loan would be used to finance a new 450,000-tonne-capacity pulp mill in South Sumatra.
"The plant will start operation at the end of 1998 or early 1999," Prajogo told reporters after the signing ceremony.
Bank of Tokyo-Mitsubishi, Fuji Bank and Sakura Finance were among the banks in the lending consortium, officials said.

Prajogo said Barito has a 55 percent stake in Tanjung Enim. Sumatera Pulp Corporation, which comprises of Nippon Paper Industries, Marubeni Corp and Overseas Economic Cooperation Fund (OECF), has 30 percent.
The rest is held by Indonesian President Suharto's eldest daughter Siti Hardianti Rukmana through her company, PT Tridan Satriaputra Indonesia.
Prajogo said the pulp plant will be located in a 193,000 hectare forest concession operated by PT Musi Hutan Persada, 60 percent owned by Barito with the rest held by state-owned PT Inhutani II.
The plant, estimated to cost $1.2 billion, will be funded by the loan and $350 million from shareholders' equity.
The plant will be built by Klockner Industrie Anlagen of Germany.
Indonesian Investment Minister Sanyoto Sastrowardoyo said domestic demand for pulp is expected to grow 13 percent a year.
Industry sources said Indonesia is expected to produce 4.4 million tonnes of pulp in 1997, compared with 3.1 million tonnes in 1996.
